CANONICAL_NAME.value: emcee 3.1.6 -- the MCMC Hammer: affine-invariant ensemble sampler (Foreman-Mackey, Hogg, Lang, Goodman)

value.lineage: Markov chain Monte Carlo (Metropolis et al. 1953; Hastings 1970) via Goodman & Weare's affine-invariant ensemble 'stretch move' (2010), implemented for astronomy (2012) and used in thousands of papers. A compact, inspectable sampler: walkers, proposals, acceptance fractions, autocorrelation time.

value.built_to: draw samples from a posterior known only up to a constant, using an ensemble of walkers that adapts to the posterior's scale and orientation
value.pressure: high-dimensional, correlated, expensive likelihoods; hand-tuned proposal scales that fail when the posterior is anisotropic
value.success_means: sample moments match the target; autocorrelation time short relative to chain length

value.pressure: hidden parameters, expensive/black-box likelihood, anisotropic scales
value.failure_condition: the chain never mixes: acceptance ~0 or ~1, autocorrelation time longer than the run, moments wrong

ANCESTRY.value: Markov chain Monte Carlo (Metropolis et al. 1953; Hastings 1970) via Goodman & Weare's affine-invariant ensemble 'stretch move' (2010), implemented for astronomy (2012) and used in thousands of papers. A compact, inspectable sampler: walkers, proposals, acceptance fractions, autocorrelation time.

value: algorithm_from: Goodman & Weare 2010; Metropolis et al. 1953

cut.note: MCMC with an ensemble of walkers where the proposal for one walker is built from the positions of the others: the stretch move draws a scale z from a density proportional to 1/sqrt(z) on [1/a, a], proposes along the line from a randomly chosen other walker through the current one, and corrects acceptance by z^(ndim-1); the ensemble is split into halves updated alternately so the 'other' walkers are fixed during a half-update (detailed balance and parallel evaluation); convergence is judged by an integrated autocorrelation time estimated with Sokal's automatic window; the whole thing needs no tuning of a proposal covariance because the moves are affine invariant

provenance.grade_basis: Techne FOSSIL_PACKET.json PROVENANCE_GRADE where issued, else the record's handoff string mapped (populated per R34; Harmonia may re-grade)

organs.human_name: StretchMove.get_proposal (stretch.py): zz = ((a - 1) rand + 1)^2 / a; factors = (ndim - 1) log zz; rint random complementary index; q = c[rint] - (c[rint] - s) zz
organs.mechanism: for each walker in the active half, pick a walker from the other half at random, draw z by squaring a uniform on [1, sqrt(a)] scaled by 1/a (which yields the density proportional to 1/sqrt(z) on [1/a, a], symmetric under z -> 1/z), and propose x' = y + z (x - y): the point on the line through y and x at stretch z; the Metropolis ratio includes z^(ndim - 1) so the move satisfies detailed balance; a = 2 by default
organs.input: the active half, the complementary half, a random state
assumptions: the ensemble's spread approximates the target's covariance, so proposals along inter-walker lines are automatically scaled and oriented (affine invariance, Goodman & Weare 2010)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: no proposal tuning; the same code works on a badly scaled, correlated posterior as on a spherical one
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: in high dimension the acceptance falls (the z^(ndim-1) factor) and the ensemble needs at least 2 ndim walkers; multimodal targets trap walkers in modes (the ensemble does not mix between modes)
organs.human_prior: Goodman & Weare 2010; Christen & Fox 2010 for the earlier 'walk' idea

organs.human_name: RedBlueMove.propose (red_blue.py 52-106): inds = all_inds % nsplits (shuffled if randomize_split); for each split: s = active, c = the others; get_proposal; compute_log_prob_fn(q) on the whole half at once; lnpdiff = factor + new - old; accept if lnpdiff > log(rand); state.update
organs.mechanism: walkers are assigned to nsplits groups (two by default, reshuffled each step); each group in turn proposes new positions using only walkers from the other groups, evaluates all its proposals' log-probabilities in one vectorised (or pooled) call, and accepts each independently by the Metropolis rule with the move's correction factor; because the complementary walkers do not move during a group's update, the update is a valid Markov transition and the group's evaluations are embarrassingly parallel
organs.output: a new state and an accepted mask
assumptions: updating all walkers simultaneously from each other would break detailed balance (Foreman-Mackey et al. 2013 section 3); two halves are enough
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: one likelihood call per half-ensemble per step: the reason the sampler scales to clusters
organs.human_prior: Foreman-Mackey, Hogg, Lang & Goodman 2013 (the parallel red-blue scheme)

organs.human_name: autocorr.integrated_time (49-130): function_1d by FFT; taus = 2 cumsum(f) - 1; auto_window(taus, c = 5): the first M with M >= c tau(M); flag if tol * tau > n
organs.mechanism: the normalised autocorrelation function of each chain (averaged over walkers) is computed by FFT; the integrated time is 2 times the running sum minus one; the window M is the first lag at which M exceeds c times the estimate at M (Sokal's rule, c = 5 by default), which balances bias against variance; if the chain is shorter than tol (50) autocorrelation times the estimate is flagged as unreliable (a warning or an exception)
assumptions: the autocorrelation function decays; the automatic window is the standard estimator (Sokal 1997); 50 tau is the recommended minimum chain length
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: a convergence diagnostic that says when it cannot be trusted
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the estimate itself is biased low for short chains, which is why tol exists
organs.human_prior: Sokal 1997 (Monte Carlo methods in statistical mechanics, the windowing lecture); Goodman & Weare 2010 acor

organs.human_name: EnsembleSampler.__init__ (ensemble.py 85-130): moves as a move, a list, or [(move, weight), ...]; the default [StretchMove()]
organs.mechanism: at each step one move is drawn from the list with the given weights and applied to the whole ensemble; the other shipped moves (walk, differential evolution, DE snooker, KDE, Gaussian) share the red-blue interface, so mixtures of proposals are a configuration
organs.input: a list of moves and weights
assumptions: mixing proposals helps on multimodal targets (DE snooker is the paper's remedy)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the sampler is a framework for ensemble moves, not one move
organs.source_boundary: the moves argument; CANDIDATE because sample's draw was not read

pressures.source_evidence: stretch.py; red_blue.py; autocorr.py; the paper's tests
pressures.condition: an organism draws samples from a log-density it can only evaluate; the density is a badly scaled, correlated Gaussian (the Rosenbrock or the 'ill-conditioned' tests) of moderate dimension; evaluations can run in parallel; the score is effective samples per evaluation and a correct statement of the autocorrelation time
pressures.failure_condition: acceptance near zero or one (untuned Metropolis), correlated chains reported as converged, or a serial evaluation pattern that wastes the parallel budget
pressures.world_punishes: isotropic random-walk Metropolis; simultaneous ensemble updates (biased); reporting tau without a length check
pressures.world_rewards: affine-invariant moves, red-blue halves, windowed autocorrelation with a reliability flag
pressures.observable_consequence: effective samples per evaluation on a 10-d Gaussian with condition number 1e4, for isotropic Metropolis vs the stretch move; bias of the simultaneous-update variant on the mean; the tol flag's false-negative rate on short chains
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: the target's covariance handed to the proposal (which the world withholds)
pressures.cheat_control: an organism given the covariance must match the stretch move's efficiency; isotropic Metropolis must fall by the condition number; the simultaneous update must bias the mean on a two-walker test: the world must show all three
pressures.purpose_separated_from_pressure: PURPOSE: affine-invariant ensemble MCMC (Foreman-Mackey et al. 2013)
